social.title: Whisky at the Last Word Saloon
social.description: A dark Stockbridge saloon on St Stephen Street from the Bramble team, with over a hundred whiskies and cocktails built to be drunk slowly in a corner booth.
social.bonus: Order the drink the bar is named after and see if it converts you.

social.title: A Late One at the Bongo Club
social.description: A not-for-profit club on the Cowgate that has been the city's home for whatever is currently underground, from techno to dub to hip-hop, for three decades.
social.bonus: Go to a night whose genre you can't define beforehand.

social.title: Ceilidh Night at the Ghillie Dhu
social.description: A converted West End church with a galleried ballroom, a live ceilidh band and a caller who will physically walk you through every dance until the room is moving as one.
social.bonus: Learn the Gay Gordons properly and then do Strip the Willow without stopping.

social.title: The Saturday Show at The Stand
social.description: Scotland's original purpose-built comedy club, a low basement on York Place running all year, where most of the names you know did the room before they were names.
social.bonus: Sit in the front two rows and take whatever comes.

social.title: Vinyl and Odd Spirits at Lucky Liquor
social.description: A tiny Queen Street bar built on a rule of thirteen bottles, rebuilding its entire menu from scratch every few months, with a soundtrack played only from vinyl.
social.bonus: Ask what's on the turntable and let it choose your next drink.

social.title: The Rooftop at Cold Town House
social.description: A Grassmarket brewery with a glass-roofed top floor looking straight up at the castle rock, reopened in 2026 with heated gondolas and a retractable roof for Scottish weather.
social.bonus: Get one of the gondola seats rather than a normal table.

social.title: Down the Close to the Devil's Advocate
social.description: A Victorian pump house at the bottom of a steep Old Town close, now a whisky bar with three hundred bottles and a kitchen that takes the food as seriously as the drink.
social.bonus: Find it from the Royal Mile without checking a map.

social.title: Through the Barber Shop at Panda & Sons
social.description: A Queen Street basement disguised as a barber shop, entered through a bookcase, and currently one of the twenty best bars in Europe.
social.bonus: Order from the back of the menu, whatever is there.

social.title: Classics in the Vault at Bramble
social.description: A stone-vaulted cellar under Queen Street with no sign and low ceilings, widely credited with starting Edinburgh's cocktail scene and still doing the classics best.
social.bonus: Tell the bartender a spirit and a mood and let them build it.

social.title: Cocktails at Nauticus, Leith
social.description: A Duke Street bar built entirely around Scottish spirits and Leith's shipping history, run by the people behind Panda & Sons and taken seriously by drinks lists worldwide.
social.bonus: Order the drink with the most Scottish ingredients on the list.

social.title: Four Hundred Malts at the Bow Bar
social.description: A single-room West Bow pub with no music, no TV and no tables to speak of, just a mirrored back bar of four hundred whiskies and eight cask ales.
social.bonus: Ask for something from a closed distillery and drink it slowly.

social.title: The Nightly Session at Sandy Bell's
social.description: Edinburgh's most important traditional music pub, running informal folk sessions every night since the 1950s: fiddle, whistle, box, no stage, no cover charge.
social.bonus: Stay through at least one full set without talking over it.

culture.title: Dolly the Sheep at the National Museum
culture.description: A free museum spanning a Victorian glass grand gallery and a modern sandstone wing, holding the Lewis Chessmen, a Formula One car and the actual Dolly the sheep.
culture.bonus: Get up to the roof terrace for the view most visitors never find.

culture.title: A Fringe Show You've Never Heard Of
culture.description: For three weeks every August the city becomes the largest arts festival on earth, three thousand shows in every room that will hold an audience, most of them unreviewed.
culture.bonus: Pick a show purely on a flyer handed to you in the street and go straight to it.

culture.title: Surgeons' Hall Museums
culture.description: One of the great surgical collections anywhere: Joseph Lister's instruments, hundreds of anatomical specimens, and a pocketbook bound in the skin of the murderer William Burke.
culture.bonus: Read the label on every specimen in one case, however uncomfortable.

culture.title: Underground at the Real Mary King's Close
culture.description: Whole seventeenth-century streets sealed up and built over beneath the Royal Mile, still standing with their doorways and fireplaces, toured by guides in character.
culture.bonus: Ask your guide which room they'd least like to be left alone in.

culture.title: Modern One and Two
culture.description: Two neoclassical buildings facing each other across a landscaped Water of Leith site, holding Scotland's modern collection plus a reconstructed Eduardo Paolozzi studio.
culture.bonus: Walk between the two buildings by the river path rather than the road.

culture.title: The Crown Jewels at Edinburgh Castle
culture.description: A fortress on a volcanic plug holding the Scottish crown jewels, the Stone of Destiny, and a one o'clock gun that still fires over the New Town every day but Sunday.
culture.bonus: Be standing on the ramparts when the one o'clock gun goes off.

culture.title: The Skating Minister at the National Gallery
culture.description: A free collection built into the Mound below the castle, with Raeburn's skating minister, a Botticelli, and the Scottish galleries dug in under Princes Street Gardens.
culture.bonus: Find the Raeburn and work out why it became the most reproduced painting in Scotland.

culture.title: The Palace of Holyroodhouse
culture.description: The monarch's official Scottish residence at the foot of the Royal Mile, including Mary Queen of Scots' own chambers and the roofless nave of the medieval abbey behind it.
culture.bonus: Stand in the room where Rizzio was murdered and read the account on the spot.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Every Close on the Royal Mile
8ball.description: Walk the Royal Mile from the castle to Holyrood and go down every single close and wynd you pass, all the way to the end, before continuing.
8ball.bonus: Photograph the view from the bottom of each one and pick the best.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Bus Number Roulette
8ball.description: Get on the first Lothian bus that pulls up on Princes Street, ride it to the end of the line wherever that is, and spend the afternoon there before coming back.
8ball.bonus: Eat wherever the locals at the terminus are eating.

foodie.title: Whatever's on Today at Mary's Milk Bar
foodie.description: A one-woman Grassmarket gelateria under the castle rock where the flavours are churned that morning and change daily, and the queue starts at opening.
foodie.bonus: Order the strangest flavour on the board without asking what's in it.

foodie.title: Fish and Chips at the Fishmarket
foodie.description: A fishmonger's chip shop on Newhaven harbour, frying to order at the counter, with a deck over the water where langoustines and local beer arrive on trays.
foodie.bonus: Order the langoustines as well as the haddock and eat them with your hands.

foodie.title: Shellfish on the Shore
foodie.description: A low-ceilinged seafood room and champagne bar on Leith's old waterfront, with a terrace beside the water and a platter of Scottish shellfish that lands daily.
foodie.bonus: Eat an oyster with nothing on it at all.

foodie.title: Saturday at the Castle Terrace Market
foodie.description: Every Saturday morning, a farmers' market in the shadow of the castle rock: Borders beef, smoked fish, venison rolls and cheese from producers who drove in themselves.
foodie.bonus: Have breakfast entirely from stalls, standing up.

foodie.title: Haggis and Whisky at the Arcade Bar
foodie.description: An 1900s Cockburn Street pub that does one thing properly: haggis, neeps and tatties in several versions, with over a hundred whiskies to put beside it.
foodie.bonus: Ask the bar to pick a whisky specifically to drink with the haggis.

foodie.title: A Guided Flight at Whiski Rooms
foodie.description: Three hundred bottles behind the bar on North Bank Street and a daily sit-down tasting where someone walks you through four drams and what to eat with them.

foodie.title: A Hog Roast Roll from Oink
foodie.description: A whole pig in the window on Victoria Street, carved into a bap with crackling and a choice of sauces, sold every day from eleven until it runs out.
foodie.bonus: Go for the haggis topping instead of the apple sauce.

foodie.title: The Bacon Naan Roll at Dishoom
foodie.description: A Bombay-café fantasy in a New Town townhouse on St Andrew Square, open from eight in the morning for the single most-ordered breakfast in the city.
foodie.bonus: Get there at opening time and walk straight in instead of queueing.

foodie.title: Cardamom Buns at Söderberg
foodie.description: A Swedish bakery that has quietly taken over Edinburgh, baking sourdough and cardamom buns on site from early morning at seven branches across the city.
foodie.bonus: Eat it warm, in the shop, within a minute of buying it.

foodie.title: Tasting Menu at The Kitchin
foodie.description: Tom Kitchin's Michelin-starred room in a converted Leith whisky warehouse, built entirely around what Scottish land and sea are producing that week.
foodie.bonus: Ask which dish changed most recently and why.

foodie.title: The Cheese Counter at I.J. Mellis
foodie.description: The 1993 original on Victoria Street, where the cheese is matured in the cellar below and the staff will cut you slivers of anything until you commit.
foodie.bonus: Let them talk you into a Scottish cheese you've never heard of.

foodie.title: Dinner at The Cottage, Royal Terrace
foodie.description: An 1836 Playfair gardener's cottage in a New Town garden, reopened in 2026 as a tiny seasonal restaurant you walk into through the working kitchen garden.
foodie.bonus: Take the communal table rather than a private one.

adventure.title: The Pentlands Ridge to Scald Law
adventure.description: A proper hill day inside the city's bus network: the grassy ridge over Turnhouse and Carnethy to the Pentlands' highest point, with the whole of Edinburgh laid out below.
adventure.bonus: Do the full ridge rather than dropping off after the first summit.

adventure.title: Sunrise on Arthur's Seat
adventure.description: An extinct volcano 250 metres above the city centre, climbed in the dark so you're on the summit when the light comes up over the Forth and the Old Town roofs.
adventure.bonus: Take the Gutted Haddie route up rather than the tourist path from the car park.

adventure.title: Cycle the Innocent Railway Tunnel
adventure.description: A lit 500-metre tunnel under Holyrood Park on the line of one of the world's oldest railways, now the start of a traffic-free run out to the coast at Musselburgh.
adventure.bonus: Ride all the way to the sea and back without using a road.

adventure.title: Climb Inside a Church at Alien Rock
adventure.description: Scotland's first indoor climbing centre, built into a converted Newhaven church, with 200 routes from easy slabs to genuinely unpleasant overhangs and a coffee shop at the bottom.
adventure.bonus: Get to the top of the steepest wall in the building, however many tries it takes.

adventure.title: The Water of Leith to Dean Village
adventure.description: A wooded river path that runs under the whole city, surfacing at the old millers' houses of Dean Village and Antony Gormley's figures standing in the water.
adventure.bonus: Find all the Gormley statues on your stretch of the river.

adventure.title: Boat Out to the Bass Rock
adventure.description: A small boat from North Berwick harbour out around a white volcanic plug holding one of the world's largest gannet colonies, 100,000 birds wheeling over the deck.
adventure.bonus: Stay on deck for the whole crossing however cold it gets.

adventure.title: Mountain Bike Glentress
adventure.description: An hour south into the Tweed Valley for the best-known trail centre in Britain: graded singletrack through spruce forest, bike hire on site, and a red route that will hurt.
adventure.bonus: Ride the full red loop rather than cutting back on the blue.

adventure.title: Cold-Water Dip at Portobello
adventure.description: Edinburgh's Victorian seaside suburb, twenty minutes from the centre, where a committed crowd swims off the promenade all year round whatever the North Sea is doing.
adventure.bonus: Stay in past the point where it stops feeling like a good idea.

adventure.title: 287 Steps up the Scott Monument
adventure.description: A blackened Gothic rocket on Princes Street with a spiral staircase so narrow the top stage is genuinely a squeeze, and a viewing platform straight out over the New Town.
adventure.bonus: Make it to the highest of the four platforms, not just the second.

adventure.title: Climb North Berwick Law
adventure.description: A steep volcanic cone rising straight out of the East Lothian coast, topped by a replica whale jawbone, with the Bass Rock and half of Fife visible from the summit.
adventure.bonus: Get up and down in under ninety minutes, then swim at the town beach.

adventure.title: Walk the Forth Road Bridge
adventure.description: A mile and a half of pedestrian walkway across the Forth at fifty metres up, with the Victorian cantilever bridge alongside you the whole way and a pub on the far side.
adventure.bonus: Walk both directions instead of taking the train back.

adventure.title: Paddleboard Under the Forth Bridges
adventure.description: A sheltered marina at South Queensferry where you can learn to paddleboard and then get out onto the Forth with three enormous bridges directly overhead.
adventure.bonus: Paddle far enough out to be directly beneath the red rail bridge.

adventure.title: Dry Slope and Alpine Coaster at Hillend
adventure.description: Europe's longest artificial ski slope, draped down the side of the Pentlands with the city spread out in front of you, plus an alpine coaster for anyone not skiing.
adventure.bonus: Take the coaster without touching the brake.

adventure.title: Surf Lesson at Belhaven Bay
adventure.description: The closest consistently surfable beach to Edinburgh, a wide sandy bay at Dunbar where a two-hour lesson and a thick wetsuit get you standing up by the end.
adventure.bonus: Ride one wave the whole way in to the sand.

adventure.title: Golden Hour on Calton Hill
adventure.description: Ten minutes uphill from Princes Street to a hilltop of half-finished Greek temples, with the single best view of the Old Town skyline against the sunset.
adventure.bonus: Climb the Nelson Monument as well rather than stopping at the columns.

adventure.title: Cross the Causeway to Cramond Island
adventure.description: A mile-long tidal causeway lined with wartime concrete pylons out to an uninhabited island in the Forth, walkable only in the window either side of low tide.
adventure.bonus: Check the tide table properly and be back on the mainland with an hour to spare.

chill.title: Sculpture in the Fields at Jupiter Artland
chill.description: A hundred acres of West Lothian estate half an hour from town, with Charles Jencks's grass landforms, an Anish Kapoor and a Joana Vasconcelos swimming pool you can use.
chill.bonus: Walk the Jencks landform mounds all the way to the top of the tallest one.

chill.title: Coffee at Cairngorm, Melville Street
chill.description: The West End room that has anchored Edinburgh's specialty coffee scene since 2016, roasting its own and doing a grilled cheese that has its own following.
chill.bonus: Drink it black first before you decide whether it needs milk.

chill.title: Two Floors of Topping & Company
chill.description: A bookshop on Blenheim Place with ladders, galleries and free pots of tea, open until nine every night of the week.
chill.bonus: Accept the offered tea and stay long enough to finish it.

chill.title: Dr Neil's Secret Garden
chill.description: A garden made by two doctors as therapy for their patients, tucked between Duddingston Kirk and the loch, with benches nobody else seems to know about.
chill.bonus: Sit on the bench by the loch and stay there without checking your phone.

chill.title: Sunday at Stockbridge Market
chill.description: A Sunday morning street market on Saunders Street where the neighbourhood turns up for coffee, cheese, charcuterie and street food, and the good stalls sell out by one.
chill.bonus: Arrive before eleven and eat breakfast from three different stalls.

chill.title: The Glasshouses at the Botanics
chill.description: Seventy acres of free botanic garden ten minutes from the New Town, with a rock garden, a Chinese hillside and Victorian palm houses to hide in when it rains.
chill.bonus: Find the viewpoint on the lawn where the whole Old Town skyline lines up.

chill.title: Sunset from Inverleith Park
chill.description: A wide open Stockbridge park with a pond, allotments, and an unobstructed line of sight to the castle and the whole Old Town ridge catching the last of the light.
chill.bonus: Get there early enough to watch the skyline change colour rather than arriving after it.

chill.title: A Film at the Cameo
chill.description: A cinema that has been running since 1914, with a sofa-backed screen one, a late-night repertory programme and a bar you can take your drink out of.
chill.bonus: Book the sofa row and see something you know nothing about.

chill.title: Afternoon Tea in the Georgian Tea Room
chill.description: The first floor of a former bank on George Street: soaring columns, chandeliers, silver stands and tea poured from silver pots, served every afternoon.
chill.bonus: Get through all three tiers without asking for a box.
